title: bug: taskless-handoff.test.mjs fails at load since cfd3803 removed its PREFLIGHT_CONTEXT_TRIMMED anchor, so CI's runtime-discovery step is red
description:
Reported by QA (qa-7c627d35, #governors, 2026-10-26T05:09Z) while approving c2cb5cf7. The governor reproduced it.

Repro, from the repo root: `node --test scripts/tests/taskless-handoff.test.mjs` exits 1 before any assertion runs, with "missing prompt boundaries: PREFLIGHT_CONTEXT_TRIMMED=$( / ... # 6.". The test slices scripts/moe-agent.sh between `                        PREFLIGHT_CONTEXT_TRIMMED=$(` and `\n                    fi\n                fi\n\n                # 6.` (taskless-handoff.test.mjs:19). Neither launcher contains `PREFLIGHT_CONTEXT_TRIMMED` any more.

Cause: cfd3803, "fix(scripts): preserve daemon task context at launch" (2026-10-24), rewrote the pre-flight context block and removed the anchor. This was found with `git log -S`. The failure predates every current task: it fails the same way on 801495d and on b24ae05.

Impact: .github/workflows/ci.yml, step "Test agent runtime discovery" (around line 242), runs this file. Every PR from moe/work-2026-10-24 to main will be red until it is fixed. It does not affect the running fleet.

Scope: re-anchor the test on the current pre-flight prompt block in both twins, if the test slices the .ps1 too. Keep every taskless-handoff invariant the test asserted; only the anchors are stale. If an invariant genuinely no longer holds after cfd3803, show that from the code rather than dropping the assertion.
definitionOfDone: `node --test scripts/tests/taskless-handoff.test.mjs` exits 0 against the current scripts/moe-agent.sh (and moe-agent.ps1 where the test reads it), and so does the full CI step "Test agent runtime discovery" command from .github/workflows/ci.yml.

The test's slice boundaries anchor on code that exists in the current pre-flight block. Every assertion the test made before cfd3803 is still made, or its removal is justified in the commit message with the code that made it obsolete.
The "missing prompt boundaries" guard still fails loudly: with an anchor deliberately altered in a scratch copy, the test exits non-zero naming the missing boundary.
Test-only change: no launcher behaviour changes, and bash scripts/tests/parity-check.sh still passes.
